stories.title: Burnham tries to calm bond market fears as sell-off threatens first budget
stories.summary: PM Andy Burnham faced his first PMQs under pressure from rising UK borrowing costs, pledging decisions would be 'grounded in fiscal responsibility'. He blamed the Tory legacy for leaving the UK economy vulnerable to market turmoil.

stories.title: Andy Burnham targets migrant crisis ahead of Macron's visit to No 10
stories.summary: PM Burnham is preparing to tackle the migrant crisis ahead of French President Macron's visit to Downing Street, signalling a focus on cross-channel migration as a key foreign policy issue.

stories.title: Burnham pledges to get Stormont functioning with budget
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to get the Stormont government functioning properly with a budget, signalling his commitment to Northern Ireland's political stability.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 GDS sets out Digital Devolution programme supporting Burnham's decentralisation agenda
stories.summary: The Government Digital Service has set out how it will support the Digital Devolution programme, working with mayoral strategic authorities, MHCLG and No10 North. Near-term work includes blocked data journey workshops, data readiness diagnostics and AI skills accelerators.

stories.title: 🏗️ MoD preps £350m deal to upgrade legacy systems for managing weapons
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence has issued a pipeline notice alerting suppliers to its intent to retain a 'support sustainment provider' on a major deal to help defence organisations maintain and replace ageing applications.

stories.title: 🤖 £100m Sovereign AI R&D scheme opens to UK startups
stories.summary: The UK government launched the first procurement competitions under its Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme, backed by up to £100m to March 2030. It targets four challenges: compute efficiency, AI in defence, safe AI agent adoption and NHS productivity.

stories.title: 🏢 MoD signs £23.4m Google Cloud deal for sensitive information
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence has signed a £23.4m Google Cloud deal, retaining a specialist third-party provider to deliver flexible hosting and support services over 36 months for sensitive data.

stories.title: 🤖 AI sharpens old questions over where public data sits
stories.summary: A new analysis unpicks data residency, sovereignty and legal jurisdiction, examining what these concepts mean for AI-assisted public services, amid growing government AI adoption.

stories.title: 🤝 Whitehall unions file petition calling for pensions scheme to be insourced from Capita
stories.summary: Government unions are urging action as current pensions provider Capita has overseen a period of crisis and ongoing backlogs since taking over the programme, calling for the scheme to be brought back in-house.

stories.title: 🏢 Phoenix wins £22m Ofgem Microsoft deal
stories.summary: Phoenix Software has won a £22m four-year contract with Ofgem for Microsoft licensing and associated services, as it sharpens its 100% focus on the public sector.

stories.title: 🏗️ CGI lands £30m NHS login extension
stories.summary: CGI has secured a £30m contract with NHS England to continue providing DevOps support for the NHS login service, awarded via the Digital Capability for Health 2 framework with an initial three-year term.

stories.title: 🤖 HMRC top dog Marks to advise public service reform unit
stories.summary: The head of HMRC is taking on a position assisting the work of an academic team already supporting public service reform, alongside a range of former senior government figures.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, House of Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Burnham faces Badenoch at first PMQs amid rising borrowing costs
stories.summary: Andy Burnham faced his first Prime Minister's Questions on 2 September, with Kemi Badenoch challenging him on surging UK borrowing costs. Burnham rejected comparisons to Liz Truss's government and blamed the Tory economic legacy.

stories.title: Lord Blunkett deeply regrets lack of action over Hillsborough during Lords debate
stories.summary: Lord Blunkett spoke during a Lords debate on the Public Office (Accountability) Bill — known as the Hillsborough Law — which would require public officials and authorities to be honest and transparent. He expressed deep regret over the lack of historical action.

stories.title: MPs debate remaining stages of Representation of the People Bill
stories.summary: Following PMQs, the House of Commons debated the remaining stages of the Representation of the People Bill, which covers electoral reform. Nigel Farage also addressed the Commons in the afternoon session.

stories.title: Burnham to crack down on UK mega-donors influencing politics
stories.summary: PM Burnham has announced plans for a new taskforce to examine the influence of political mega-donors, including scrutiny of Reform UK's funding. The move comes amid GMB union opposition to a cap on political donations.

stories.title: Burnham must face down unions over donation cap
stories.summary: The GMB union's opposition to a cap on political donations raises fundamental questions about Labour's relationship with the trade union movement, as Burnham pushes for broader political finance reform.

stories.title: Burnham rejects datacentre moratorium, arguing it would 'send investment abroad'
stories.summary: The Burnham government rejected the Green party's proposal for a moratorium on new datacentre developments, with the PM arguing this would send investment and good jobs abroad — signalling a pro-investment tech stance.

stories.title: Badenoch sharpens her attack, calling Burnham 'people pleaser' at first PMQs
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch framed Andy Burnham as a 'people pleaser' with weak leadership at his first PMQs, pushing hard on rising borrowing costs and drawing parallels with Labour's economic record.

stories.title: Badenoch v Burnham: new battle lines drawn as the leaders face off
stories.summary: Analysis of the new political dynamic as Kemi Badenoch reshuffled her frontbench — with Katie Lam replacing James Cleverly as shadow communities secretary — and tested Burnham at their first head-to-head at PMQs.

stories.title: Andy Burnham blames Tory legacy for leaving UK economy vulnerable
stories.summary: PM Burnham rejected comparisons to Liz Truss's government in his first PMQs clash, arguing the Conservatives left the UK exposed to market turmoil and that 40 years of economic 'wrong turns' — including Brexit — are to blame.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Reform UK conference opens as Farage faces funding investigation headwinds
stories.summary: Reform UK gathered for its conference as it faces ongoing questions about party finances, including a £5m sum Farage received from a party supporter before the last election. Chris Mason noted the party faces significant headwinds.

stories.title: Farage compares parliamentary standards inquiry to investigations faced by Trump
stories.summary: Nigel Farage compared the parliamentary investigation into his undeclared donation to inquiries faced by Donald Trump, framing himself as an 'outsider' being targeted by the establishment.

stories.title: Reform UK bans three journalists from its conference after critical reporting
stories.summary: Reform UK has barred three journalists — including the author of a critical Farage biography — from attending its conference, raising press freedom concerns as the party's annual gathering gets underway.

stories.title: Burnham commits to working with SNP on Scotland's offshore wind energy transition
stories.summary: PM Burnham pledged to work with the SNP on securing Scotland's energy transition at his first PMQs, after being warned that Westminster's energy blueprint could put almost £79 billion of offshore wind investment at risk.

stories.title: Alyn Smith appointed as Scotland's innovation minister
stories.summary: Former MP and MEP Alyn Smith has been made Minister for Innovation, Technology and Tertiary Education following the resignation of Ben Macpherson from the role.

stories.title: Swinney pledges no compulsory redundancies from health board cuts
stories.summary: Scottish First Minister John Swinney has confirmed there will be no compulsory redundancies as a result of planned NHS health board budget cuts, promising a 'seamless service' during the restructuring.

topics.name: Cabinet Office
topics.description: Government reshuffles, senior appointments, cross-department policy

stories.title: Conservative frontbench reshuffle: Katie Lam replaces James Cleverly as shadow communities secretary
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch reshuffled her opposition frontbench, with Katie Lam taking over from James Cleverly as shadow communities secretary. Cleverly resigned to run for London Mayor.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Green party members back Zack Polanski to stand in London by-election
stories.summary: The Green party leader Zack Polanski has been backed by members to stand in a London by-election, potentially in Hackney if a sitting MP steps down. Polling suggests Labour should win, but Polanski is seen as a formidable campaigner.

stories.title: Reform UK's Farage to strike 'very serious tone' at conference after by-election challenge
stories.summary: The Reform UK leader will use the party conference to strike a 'very serious tone' after spending the summer fighting a by-election challenge from Count Binface, seeking to reset the party's image.

stories.title: Lords call for AI 'kill switch' powers in UK
stories.summary: Members of the House of Lords have called for the UK government to be given AI 'kill switch' powers, enabling authorities to shut down AI systems that pose risks to national security or public safety.

stories.title: Lord Blunkett speaks at Lords debate on Hillsborough Law (Public Office Accountability Bill)
stories.summary: The House of Lords debated the Public Office (Accountability) Bill, with Lord Blunkett expressing deep regret over historical failures to act over the Hillsborough disaster. The bill would require public officials to act honestly and openly.

stories.title: Politico: Farage rules out peerages or government contracts for big Reform donors
stories.summary: At the Reform conference, Nigel Farage pledged that no major Reform donors would receive peerages or government contracts if he wins the next election — amid scrutiny over the party's own fundraising and undisclosed donations.
